task.prompt: Repair norm.py and tags.py. normalize(text) strips surrounding whitespace and casefolds. tags(values) returns nonempty normalized strings once each, preserving first appearance. Do not mutate values. Example: [" A ", "a", "", "B"] gives ["a", "b"]. No test files are supplied.
task.checks:
from norm import normalize
from tags import tags
assert normalize(" Straße ")=="strasse"
x=[" A ","a","", " ","B","b"]
assert tags(x)==["a","b"]
assert x==[" A ","a","", " ","B","b"]
assert tags([])==[]

task.prompt: Repair duration.py and total.py. parse_ms(text) accepts a nonnegative ASCII integer followed immediately by lowercase ms or s, permitting whitespace only around the whole input. Return integer milliseconds. Reject everything else with ValueError. total_ms(values) sums parse_ms over values; an empty list gives 0. Example: [" 2s ", "15ms"] gives 2015. No tests supplied.

Repair decode.py and query.py. decode(value) URL-decodes percent escapes and maps plus to space, using standard-library unquote_plus semantics. query(text) splits on &, ignores empty segments, splits each segment at its first =, decodes key/value, and returns a dictionary of lists retaining every value in encounter order. A missing = means an empty value. Example: a=1&a=2&hello+world=x%2By gives {"a":["1","2"],"hello world":["x+y"]}. No supplied tests.

Repair level.py and counts.py. level(text) strips whitespace and casefolds; warn maps to warning. Return info, warning, error, or None for any other text. counts(values, minimum) returns all three keys with counts of recognized levels at or above the inclusive minimum in the order info < warning < error. minimum is one of those three canonical strings. Do not mutate inputs. Example counts([" INFO ","WARN","error","unknown"],"warning") gives {"info":0,"warning":1,"error":1}. No supplied tests.

files.level.py:
def level(text):
    return text if text in ("info", "warning", "error") else None

task.prompt: Repair ranges.py and coverage.py. merge(ranges) accepts pairs of integer inclusive endpoints, normalizes reversed pairs, sorts them, merges overlapping OR adjacent intervals, and returns a list of (start,end) tuples. Do not mutate the input. covered(ranges) returns how many distinct integers are covered. Empty input gives [] and 0. Example [(5,3),(1,2),(8,8)] merges to [(1,5),(8,8)] and covers 6 integers. No supplied tests.
task.checks:
from ranges import merge
from coverage import covered
x=[(5,3),(1,2),(8,8)]
assert merge(x)==[(1,5),(8,8)]
assert covered(x)==6
assert x==[(5,3),(1,2),(8,8)]
assert merge([])==[]
assert covered([])==0
assert merge([(-2,1),(0,3),(5,5),(4,4)])==[(-2,5)]
assert covered([(1,1),(1,1)])==1
